Shengzhou Qiang

Ph.D. candidate in Computer Science, University at Buffalo

I work on transactional distributed databases: concurrency control, consistency protocols, and the fault-injection testing that shows whether a system keeps its guarantees.

Most of my work ends in a measurement or a failing test. I have re-measured published results, reproduced a deadlock across thousands of randomized fault schedules, and landed fixes in an open-source Rust codebase.

Open to Summer 2027 internships in database and storage engines, distributed infrastructure, reliability, and inference serving. Graduating June 2028.

Research

SONIC

First author · under review

Read-only transactions without replication-critical designs. I prove those designs unnecessary and demonstrate it in two systems, one built on TAPIR in C++ and one on COPS-SNOW, validated under crashes and partitions with Jepsen suites I wrote.

TxJBOF

Lead student · in progress

Concurrency control for storage built from a DPU and a shelf of NVMe SSDs. I reproduced Scalio (OSDI '25) on CloudLab with RDMA, SPDK and NVMe-oF, then designed a client-side write path that takes the DPU's weak CPU off every write. Evaluated on emulated NVMe so far.

Juicer

Co-author · in submission

A gRPC-Go interceptor layer that reorders in-flight transaction messages by timestamp. It cuts P99 latency by up to 75% and aborts by up to 85% for strictly serializable databases, with zero database-code changes.

EaaS

Top contributor · 2023 – 2025

An end-to-end evaluation framework for distributed storage in C++ and gRPC. I built its YCSB and TPC-C workload engine and the CockroachDB and Cassandra adapters. Our cross-region AWS measurements refuted EPaxos's published 3× throughput claim (1–1.5× measured).

PRC

Co-author · in submission

Consistency testing that turns community-known correctness pitfalls, such as timestamp inversion, into targeted tests that complement random exploration tools like Jepsen.

Open source

Nervos Fiber

2 fixes merged upstream

A Rust payment-channel network. I wrote a Jepsen suite for it and reproduced a channel deadlock: 1,030 occurrences in 6,000 randomized fault schedules before a root-cause fix I proposed, 0 after. The maintainers chose a protocol redesign for that issue; two other fixes of mine are merged upstream.

fiber-jepsenDeadlock #1561PR #1675PR #1700

agent-faultlab

Author · MIT

A fault-injection lab for AI trading agents: a deterministic stand-in for a broker API with price replay, injected timeouts with late commits, and a checker that catches orders filled twice.
